assessment_summary: I validated the Interaktive Gartenkarte installation against the guide's 'Lokales Dev-Setup' method (the method actually executed). (1) Prerequisites: PHP 8.4.26 with all required extensions (sqlite3, mbstring, xml, curl, fileinfo), Composer 2.10.3, Node v22.23.3, npm 10.9.9 — all satisfy the guide; PHP 8.4 instead of 8.2 is justified because composer.lock pins symfony packages requiring php>=8.4 and the guide's Herd section explicitly allows '8.3, 8.4 oder höher'. (2) Installation artifacts: vendor/ (composer install), node_modules (npm install), .env created from .env.example with a generated APP_KEY, database/database.sqlite created and migrated (migrate:status all 'Ran'; 9 tables verified directly via PDO). (3) Runtime: the composer dev stack (artisan serve :8000, queue:listen, pail, Vite :5173) is running; port 8000 returned HTTP 200 with the Inertia 'MainPage' (the interactive garden map) whose props carry 37 sensor markers and nav elements; port 5173 returned 200 for the Vite client and for every module reachable from MainPage.vue — I traced the full import chain (MainPage → Navigation, Sensor, Ochsi, HomeInfoCard, SensorCard → InfoCard, types/Sensor) and every file exists and is served. (4) Core function: the guide states sensor data loads live from opendata.wuerzburg.de; I verified this end-to-end via GET /api/sensors/wetterstation/data which returned HTTP 200 with genuine current readings (10.6 °C, 93.4 % humidity, 4 mm rain, 98 W/m² radiation), proving the backend → external open-data API → rendered HTML data path works. /api/home-info-card-text and /up also returned 200. (5) Known limitation assessment: two Vue components (UserInfo.vue, UserMenuContent.vue) are missing from the upstream repository itself (git ls-tree on commit 7edb795 = main confirms they were never committed; they are not gitignored). I verified they are unreachable from the only routed page (MainPage): they are imported only by NavUser.vue, which is imported only by AppSidebar.vue/AppHeader.vue, which are used only by layouts consumed by Dashboard.vue — and Dashboard.vue has no route (route:list shows a single app route GET /). Therefore the missing files break only `npm run build` (the production deployment path, an alternative method not executed) and an unrouted page; they are a source defect the installer could not and should not have fabricated, and they do not impair the operational dev installation. Limitations of my validation: no headless browser was available, so frontend rendering was verified by module-graph resolution via the Vite dev server rather than DOM execution; ss/netstat were unavailable so port checks were done via direct HTTP requests (all successful). Conclusion: every step of the executed installation method completed, and the software demonstrably operates as described in the guide (app reachable at http://localhost:8000, Vite assets at :5173, live sensor data flowing), so the outcome is success.
